author: vansh_sahay
content:
following the last frames breakout, had some thoughts on the inline sigs plan - if the hash covers the raw signature bytes, stripping them for aggregation later changes the hash, and anything that saw the tx before stripping (mempool, RPC users, receipts) now points at a different tx, keeping the signature outside from day one avoids this, because the tx's identity never included it

if we keep it inside, i don't think we need SSZ particularly to fix this i think we can stay on RLP and hash keccak(sig) in the sig's slot instead of the bytes, similar to 4844 for blobs and the sig hash already uses for the length, a stripped tx then carries 32 bytes and keeps its hash. I tried this in geth with my leanSPHINCS impl where 7841 -> 126 bytes per tx and got the same tx hash and same tx root, SSZ would give the same result but like <@827653956955406406> mentioned in the call, it adds extra scope for each client to implement
